name: Plane
tagline: A modern issue tracker with boards, cycles and pages
description: An issue and project tracker in the style of current commercial tools: work items in list, board, calendar, spreadsheet and timeline views, cycles for sprints, modules for larger pieces of work, and pages for notes and specifications.
licenseNote: The Community edition is AGPL-3.0. A separate commercial edition, self-hosted or in Plane's cloud, adds features such as time tracking, custom work item types, SAML and OpenID Connect sign-in and some importers. The split has changed more than once: check the current comparison before choosing an edition.
backing: Plane Software, Inc. (US), a venture-backed company funded by paid plans

maturity.rationale: Popular and developed quickly, with frequent releases. Still young: features and the line between free and paid editions keep moving, and upgrades occasionally need manual steps.

selfHosting.summary: An official script sets up the Docker Compose stack: web, API, workers, PostgreSQL, a cache and object storage. It runs on a small server; the care goes on backing up the database and uploads, outgoing mail, and reading release notes before upgrading.

managedHosting.label: Plane Cloud
managedHosting.note: Run by the developers; free tier, then paid per user

strengths: Feels current: fast boards, keyboard shortcuts and the views people know from commercial trackers
Cycles, modules and pages cover sprints, larger initiatives and written specs in one tool
A hosted service with a free tier, so a team can try it before running it
weaknesses: Open core, with a moving line: time tracking, custom types and enterprise sign-in are in paid editions
Young: fewer integrations and reports than Jira, and the occasional rough upgrade
Workflows are simple states rather than Jira's configurable transitions
Several services to run and back up when self-hosted

featureNotes.custom-workflows: Custom states are free; custom types and properties are in paid editions
featureNotes.jira-import: An importer exists; check which edition includes it
featureNotes.task-app-import: An Asana importer exists; check which edition includes it
featureNotes.free-sso: Sign-in with Google, GitHub or GitLab is free; SAML and OpenID Connect are paid
